in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about one child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old. I'm hoping to adopt him, but he hasn't moved in with me yet. Can I still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your current situation a bit better.

**Has Alex come to live with you yet, or is he still living elsewhere while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't come to live with me yet. He's still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process. But I am contributing money towards his upkeep - I help out financially with things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you - you do not have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the key requirement is that the child needs to have come to live with you first.

Since Alex hasn't moved in with you yet and is still living elsewhere, let me ask:

**Are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards Alex's upkeep - for example on food, clothes or pocket money? And do you know approximately how much you're contributing?**

This is important because you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child, and you're usually considered responsible if either you live with them OR you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am contributing towards his upkeep. I pay £30 a week - I help with things like clothes, shoes, and other things he needs. Is that enough to qualify?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Let me clarify one more important detail to make a proper assessment:

**Where is Alex currently living? Is he living with another family member, in foster care, or in some other arrangement while the adoption process is ongoing?**

This will help me determine whether you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit at this stage, before he moves in with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living with another family at the moment - not with any of my family members. It's just a temporary arrangement while we work through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Now let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex - for example, the family he's currently living with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the family he's living with isn't claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one final question:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's living with this other family?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I'm the one providing the financial support for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✅ **You meet the responsibility requirement**: Even though Alex hasn't moved in with you yet, you are considered responsible for him because you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep (for clothes, shoes, and other necessities). This exceeds the current Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child.

✅ **Other eligibility criteria are met**:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

The Child Benefit rules state that you're usually responsible for a child if either you live with them OR you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them. You meet this second condition.

**What to do next**: You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Once he does move in with you to complete the adoption, your eligibility will continue (and likely be even more straightforward), but you don't need to wait for that to happen before claiming.

If you have any other questions, please let me know!
